question: What feature of Indus Valley town planning indicates advanced civic amenities and engineering skills of the civilisation?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Drainage systems**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indus Valley Civilization featured advanced drainage systems, showcasing their engineering expertise and focus on urban planning.
 
• Each house in cities like Mohenjo-Daro and Harappa had access to a private or public drainage system connected to larger drains in the streets.
 
• The drains were covered with bricks and had inspection holes for regular cleaning and maintenance.
 
• The systematic layout of these drainage systems ensured hygienic living conditions and effective waste management, demonstrating a deep understanding of sanitation.
 
• The presence of these systems indicates the importance given to civic amenities by the Indus Valley people.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Town Planning in the Indus Valley Civilization:**

 
 
• The cities were planned in a grid pattern, with streets intersecting at right angles.
 
• Buildings were constructed using standardized baked bricks, indicating advanced architectural techniques.
 
 
 
• **Great Bath of Mohenjo-Daro:**
 
 
• It was a large, rectangular tank believed to be used for ritual bathing, showcasing advanced waterproofing and drainage technology.
 
 
 
• **Water Management:**
 
 
• Wells and reservoirs were common features, ensuring access to clean water across the cities.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Urban Planning:**
 
 
• The structured planning reflects a high level of administrative control and social organization in the civilization.
